[Jumping Knowledge Networks](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/xu18c/xu18c.pdf) (Xu et al., 2018) provide a direct conceptual precedent: collect intermediate representations and aggregate through concatenation, max pooling, or node-dependent LSTM attention. The attention variant softmax-normalizes scores across layers, producing an input-dependent weighted sum. [ELMo](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1202/) (Peters et al., 2018) instead learns task-specific scalar softmax weights plus a scale parameter; these weights are shared across tokens. Its representations are contextual, but its layer weights are static.

[Dynamic Layer Aggregation](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/3772/3650) (Dou et al., 2019) is an especially close precedent for position-dependent mixing: its simple dynamic-combination baseline computes position-specific softmax layer weights using a feed-forward network over hidden states. More elaborate variants use capsule routing-by-agreement. Dynamic aggregation outperformed static aggregation on the studied translation tasks; this does not establish gains for recommendation. Within the NextItNet setting, [SkipRec](https://cdn.aaai.org/ojs/16518/16518-13-20012-1-2-20210518.pdf) (Chen et al., 2021) supplies related user-adaptive depth selection, although it selects/skips residual layers rather than pooling their outputs through attention.

For a causal convolutional recommender, position-dependent softmax mixing is therefore best framed as adapting established layer aggregation to different receptive-field depths. Recommended ablations: final layer only; uniform average of the same intermediate states; learned static softmax weights shared across users/positions; input-dependent softmax weights. Keep backbone, normalization, output scale, training budget and selection protocol matched. Dynamic versus static isolates the contribution of conditioning; static versus uniform isolates learned layer preference. An additional position-only gate distinguishes absolute-position effects from history-dependent adaptation. All variants can remain single jointly trained networks.
